note: Block p00, 33 people who first served 2000-01 to 2009-10. No Talisman exists online for this era, confirmed by three earlier researchers; the Herald spring election specials are the only portrait seam.

name: Brittany Fausey
fact: Fausey stood for a senate seat in the March 2004 election hoping to be appointed speaker of the senate. The Herald described her as a junior from Jeffersonville, Indiana, in her third year in SGA and then coordinator of committees, having previously co-chaired the public relations committee. She was a corporate and organisation communication major, a member of Alpha Omicron Pi and a Spirit Master, and said she would work against plus/minus grading.

src.label: College Heights Herald, Decision 2004 election section, 16 March 2004, p. 3

note: NO PHOTOGRAPH, Brittany Fausey: her senate candidate block in the Decision 2004 section prints the words Photo not available where the mugshot would be. That is the one election special in which she stood, so this route is closed for her.

name: Stacey Taylor
fact: Stacey and Natalie Taylor were identical twins from Paducah, by way of Michigan, who came to Western in 1999, roomed together in Central Hall, both majored in accounting and shared five of their six classes. The Herald's feature on them in April 2001 lists student government among the activities they did together, with Omega Phi Alpha service sorority, the Accounting Club, Campus Scouts and the Latter Day Saints Student Association, where they were co-presidents. Stacey was the elder by sixty seconds.

src.label: College Heights Herald, Vol. 76, No. 54, 24 April 2001, pp. 10-11

name: Natalie Taylor
fact: Natalie Taylor was the younger of the identical Taylor twins by sixty seconds, an accounting major who lived with her sister Stacey in Central Hall and belonged to the same organisations, student government among them. She became engaged in February 2001 to Aaron Bergquist, a soldier at Fort Campbell then serving in Kosovo.

src.label: College Heights Herald, Vol. 76, No. 54, 24 April 2001, pp. 10-11

name: Angelika Masero
fact: Masero graduated from WKU and the Honors College in 2010 with degrees in journalism and German. In May 2014 she was one of seven WKU students and graduates honoured by the Fulbright US Student Program, the most in the university's history, receiving an English Teaching Assistantship to Germany. She was then College and Career Readiness Counselor at Iroquois High School in Jefferson County.

name: Dana Lockhart
fact: Lockhart, a junior from Hendersonville, Tennessee, ran for executive vice president of SGA in the spring of 2003 and was the only candidate for the office, campaigning alongside Jessica Martin for vice president of administration and John Bradley for president. He told the Herald he wanted an SGA in which every student felt comfortable raising a concern, and said he would press for the renovation of Keen Hall and Pearce-Ford Tower.

src.label: College Heights Herald, Vol. 78, No. 47, 20 March 2003, p. 6

name: Dana Lockhart
fact: A year earlier, in the April 2002 election, Lockhart ran for vice president against John Bradley on a platform of substance over style. He said SGA could not represent students if it did not talk to them, that the way it awarded organisational aid needed an overhaul, and that the organisation was in need of constitutional reform.

src.label: College Heights Herald, Vol. 77, No. 49, 4 April 2002, p. 9

note: NO PHOTOGRAPH, Dana Lockhart: he has two full candidate profiles in the Herald, 4 April 2002 (Vol. 77 No. 49, p. 9) and 20 March 2003 (Vol. 78 No. 47, p. 6), and neither carries a mugshot. Both pages were rendered and checked. The 28 March 2002 election special runs mugshot panels only for the vice president of finance and the five vice president of administration candidates, not for the executive vice president race he was in. He also signed two letters to the editor, 4 December 2001 (dlsc_ua_records/9131) and, with Brandon Copeland and Matthew Pava, 31 August 2004 (dlsc_ua_records/9405). Those are text.

name: Austin Bernard Wingate
fact: The Herald reported in March 2012 that Wingate had served three years in SGA, two as a senator and one as speaker of the senate. He was not in SGA that year because he was president of the WKU chapter of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People, and he stood for the SGA presidency against Cory Dodds and Corey Johnson on a platform of diversity, scholar and Greek outreach and better campus parking. Dodds won.

src.label: College Heights Herald, Vol. 87, No. 29, 20 March 2012, p. 8

note: IDENTITY RESOLVED, Austin Wingate: the 2006-2010 researcher left open whether the Austin Wingate who ran for president in March 2012 was the worklist's 2008-09 senator. The 20 March 2012 candidate story settles it - it says he had served three years in SGA, two as a senator and one as speaker of the senate, before standing down for a year, which places his first senate year in 2008-09.

NO PHOTOGRAPH, Austin Wingate, from the 2012 election: the three-candidate story of 20 March 2012 is text only, with no mugshots, and the page's one photograph is of a band at SKyPAC. The Herald's own picture of the result, 30 March 2012, is a group frame in the SGA office whose caption names Cory Dodds, Cain Alvey and Keyana Boka but gives no positions, so it identifies nobody. There is a wku.edu-era Herald photograph of a WKU graduate Austin Wingate at a politics forum on 23 February 2017 (wkuherald.com), but it is a two-person frame with no positional marker.

FLAG FOR THE EDITOR, Elizabeth White and Lizzy White. The archive carries Elizabeth White as a 2004-05 senator and Lizzy White as a 2005-06 senator, and they are very probably the same person under two forms of one name. The Herald's 2005 election special (15 March 2005, p. 3C) calls her a Nashville sophomore in her second semester in SGA, on the campus improvement committee and vice chair of public relations, and a member of Alpha Delta Pi and the Public Relations Student Society of America. Second semester in March 2005 means she joined in the autumn of 2004, which is the year the roster calls her Elizabeth. The same mugshot has now been filed for both rows, deliberately, so that the duplication is visible rather than hidden. This was not merged in the data, per the rule to flag and not fix.

name: Elizabeth White
fact: White, a sophomore from Nashville, ran for a senate seat in March 2005 in her second semester in SGA. She sat on the campus improvement committee and was vice chair of public relations, argued that students had a right to see faculty evaluations, and worked to get recycling bins put on campus, promoting the idea through her own committee and planning an awareness push during Earth week. She belonged to Alpha Delta Pi and the Public Relations Student Society of America.

src.label: College Heights Herald, SGA election special, 15 March 2005, p. 3C

name: Cherieth L. Lineweaver
fact: Lineweaver ran unopposed for a second term as administrative vice president in the SGA election of 3 and 4 April 2007 and took 1,231 votes. She told the Herald she was ready to carry on the work she had been doing all semester and wanted to keep improving Organizational Aid. She was elected alongside Jeanne Johnson as president and Johnathon Boles as executive vice president.

src.label: College Heights Herald, Vol. 82, No. 44, 5 April 2007, p. 6

name: Cherieth L. Lineweaver
fact: Her re-election bid was announced in the Herald's account of candidate filing a week earlier, which named her as the sitting administrative vice president standing again while Johnathon Boles, the speaker of the senate, ran for the presidency against Jeanne Johnson and senator Kendrick Bryan.

src.label: College Heights Herald, Vol. 82, No. 41, 27 March 2007, p. 1

note: NO PHOTOGRAPH, Cherieth Lineweaver: both 2007 issues that name her were downloaded and the relevant pages rendered. The candidate-filing story of 27 March 2007 runs a photograph of three other students, and the results page of 5 April 2007 runs one photograph, of the defeated candidate Kendrick Bryan. The 2007 election had no mugshot panel; the Herald's candidate panels ran 2001-2005 and again from 2008. The 2006 issues covering the election she first won (dlsc_ua_records/3694 and 3695) do not name her at all, so she may have come to the office by appointment during 2006-07 rather than by election, which would explain her absence from the 2006 coverage.

SOURCE WORTH MINING, the Spirit Masters scrapbooks in the WKU Archives student organisation collection. UA12/2/16 for 2004-2005 is digitalcommons.wku.edu/stu_org/327 and for 2001-2002 is stu_org/323; there is a 2006-2007 Spirit Masters item at stu_org/529. Pages 4 and 5 of the 2004-05 scrapbook photograph the group's display board, which pastes every member's studio headshot beside a handwritten name, year, major and home town. That is an identification the archive's rules accept, and the portraits are colour studio work rather than newsprint halftones. The scrapbooks carry no text layer, so they have to be looked at rather than searched. This is where the Brittany Fausey portrait came from, and it is the strongest portrait source found anywhere in the 2000-2010 block.
